text:
Predicates:
AdmiresMax(x) ::: Max admires design style x.
Style(x) ::: x is a design style.
InterestingGeometries(x) ::: x has interesting geometries.
ZahaHadid(x) ::: x is a Zaha Hadid design style.
KellyWearstler(x) ::: x is a Kelly Wearstler design style.
Evocative(x) ::: x is evocative.
Dreamy(x) ::: x is dreamy.
Design(x) ::: x is a design.
MaxDesign(x) ::: x is a design by Max.
Brutalist(x) ::: x is a brutalist building.
HasDesignStyle(x, y) ::: x has design style y.

Premises:
∀x (AdmiresMax(x) → Style(x)) ::: All styles Max adores have interesting geometries.
∀x (AdmiresMax(x) ∧ Style(x) → ¬Brutalist(x)) ::: No style Max adores is a brutalist style.
∀x (AdmiresMax(x) ∧ Style(x) → (ZahaHadid(x) ∨ KellyWearstler(x))) ::: All styles Max adores are either Zaha Hadid's or Kelly Wearstler's.
∀x (AdmiresMax(x) ∧ Style(x) ∧ KellyWearstler(x) → Evocative(x)) ::: Kelly Wearstler styles Max adores are evocative.
∀x (AdmiresMax(x) ∧ Style(x) ∧ KellyWearstler(x) → Dreamy(x)) ::: Kelly Wearstler styles Max adores are dreamy.
∀x (MaxDesign(x) ∧ AdmiresMax(x) ∧ InterestingGeometries(x) → (Brutalist(x) ∧ Evocative(x))) ::: If Max's design has interesting geometries, then it is a brutalist building and evocative.

Conclusion:
∃x (MaxDesign(x) ∧ Brutalist(x)) ::: A design by Max is a brutalist building.
